what_its_for: This medicine gives your child important vitamins (like A, C, D, and B vitamins) that help their body grow strong and stay healthy. It also contains fluoride, a mineral that helps protect your child's teeth from cavities and makes tooth enamel stronger. It is used when your child's drinking water does not have enough fluoride added to it.
how_to_take: Give this medicine by mouth exactly as your child's doctor prescribed. It usually comes as liquid drops that you can measure with the dropper provided. You can place the drops directly in your child's mouth, mix them into food, or add them to juice or water. Do NOT mix with milk or formula, as this can stop the fluoride from working properly. Give it at the same time each day to help you remember. Always use the measuring dropper that comes with the medicine — never use a household spoon.
dosing: The dose depends on your child's age and how much fluoride is already in your local drinking water. Your doctor will tell you the exact amount to give. A common starting dose for infants and young children is 1 mL (1 dropperful) once a day, but always follow your doctor's specific instructions. Do not give more than prescribed.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, give it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with the regular schedule. Do NOT give two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep the bottle tightly closed and away from direct sunlight and heat. Do not freeze. Keep this medicine out of reach of children. Do not use after the expiration date printed on the label.
what_to_avoid: Do not mix the drops with milk, dairy products, or formula because they can block the fluoride from being absorbed. Avoid giving your child other vitamins or supplements that also contain fluoride at the same time, as too much fluoride can cause white spots or streaking on the teeth (a condition called dental fluorosis). Check all other vitamins and supplements your child takes with your doctor or pharmacist. Do not give more than the prescribed amount.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your child's doctor right away if you notice: white, brown, or black spots or streaking on your child's teeth; signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, hives, swelling of the face or throat, or trouble breathing; nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, or diarrhea that does not go away; unusual weakness or muscle pain; or if your child accidentally swallows a large amount of the medicine. Also call your doctor if you move to a new area, as the fluoride level in your new water supply may be different and the dose may need to change.
when_it_works: The vitamins in this medicine start supporting your child's health right away with regular daily use. The fluoride works gradually over time to strengthen teeth and prevent cavities. You may not notice obvious changes, but consistent daily use is important for your child's long-term dental and overall health. Do not stop giving it without talking to your doctor.
special_populations: This medicine is made specifically for infants and young children. The dose is carefully based on age and local water fluoride levels, so always follow your doctor's instructions. Tell your doctor if your child has any kidney problems, as this may affect how fluoride is processed. Let your doctor know about all other vitamins, supplements, or medicines your child takes. This product is not meant for adults. Pregnant or breastfeeding mothers should speak to their own doctor about their personal vitamin and fluoride needs.
